column1: # console_only_probes.tsv -- WHICH PROBES ARE LEGITIMATELY UNMEASURABLE
# WITHOUT A HUMAN AT THE CONSOLE.
# LAUNCH DIRECTIVE item 3 (CLAUDE.md, Andy, 2026-09-07), verbatim:
#   "Andy is asked to walk ONLY when the thin walk reports 0 FAIL and the only
#    CANNOT-RUNs are TCC/GUI items. Never before."
# That sentence needs a list, and until this file there was none. run_box_walk.sh
# exited 0 on FAIL=0 && BROKEN=0 regardless of how many probes reported
# CANNOT-RUN, so a walk where half the instruments shrugged reported the same
# success as a walk where every one of them measured. This file is the half of
# the directive the code could not read.
# THE RULE, and it is the whole file:
#   a probe listed here with surface tcc or gui  -> its CANNOT-RUN is expected
#       on an ssh walk, because the measurement genuinely needs a human logged
#       in at the machine. It does not make the walk non-clean.
#   ANY OTHER PROBE -> its CANNOT-RUN is COVERAGE LOST. The walk exits 3 and
#       names it.
# SILENCE IS NEVER AN EXEMPTION. A probe that does not appear here is NOT
# exempt, and so is an absent or unreadable file: run_box_walk.sh then treats
# every CANNOT-RUN as coverage lost and says so on the console. Both failure
# directions land on "the walk is not clean", which is the only safe one.
# A TYPO IS NOT AN EXEMPTION EITHER. Only the exact strings tcc and gui are
# read as a surface. Any other value in column 2 leaves the probe non-exempt.
# ⚠️ THIS FILE SHIPS WITH ZERO EXEMPT PROBES, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT,
# NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Taken 2026-09-23 over the 29 probes in probes/:
#   /usr/bin/grep -h probe_cannot_run probes/*.sh \
#     | /usr/bin/grep -Eic 'tcc|full disk|screen recording|at the console|gui'   -> 5
#   POSITIVE CONTROL, same corpus, same pipeline:
#   /usr/bin/grep -h probe_cannot_run probes/*.sh | /usr/bin/grep -ic ssh        -> 21
# The control proves the search resolves. All 5 subject hits were then read and
# all 5 are the substring "gui" inside ordinary English (guidance, distinguish,
# arguing); NONE is about TCC or a GUI. Every real CANNOT-RUN reason in the
# suite is ssh reachability, an absent prerequisite, or a stated ambiguity, and
# an operator sitting at the box fixes none of those by being there.
# So on the evidence available today, NO probe qualifies, and the honest list is
# empty. Adding the first row is a deliberate act with a reason next to it,
# which is the point: an exemption someone had to write down can be argued with,
# and one that is merely the default cannot.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated, exactly three):
#   probe     the probe file name without .sh, exactly as the record names it
#   surface   tcc | gui -- what specifically needs the console
#   why       what a human at the machine can do that ssh cannot
# probe
